definition: The broad group of peoples and cultures of central Mexico who speak Nahuatl or share its heritage. The Mexica of Tenochtitlan were one Nahua people among many, and Nahua communities still live in Mexico today.

The Nahua people who founded Tenochtitlan on an island in Lake Texcoco and became the core of the Aztec Empire. The name 'Aztec' comes from Aztlan, their legendary homeland; 'Mexica' is the name they used for themselves.

The present world age in Nahua cosmology, named Four Movement (Nahui Ollin), when Nanahuatzin became the sun at Teotihuacan and the other gods gave their lives to set it moving. It is expected to end in a great earthquake.
The main temple of Tenochtitlan, a stepped pyramid with twin shrines to Huitzilopochtli, god of war and the sun, and Tlaloc, god of rain. Its excavated remains lie in the center of Mexico City.

The cold underworld of the Nahua dead, ruled by Mictlantecuhtli and Mictecacihuatl. Souls journeyed through nine levels, and Quetzalcoatl descended there to fetch the bones from which new people were made.
The paradise of Tlaloc, a green and abundant realm where those who died by drowning, lightning or water-related illness went. It was a blessed afterlife, not a place of punishment.

A handwritten book, usually folded or bound, made by Mesoamerican or colonial artists. Pre-conquest codices were painted on deer hide or paper; colonial codices recorded myths and history in Nahuatl and Spanish.
A Nahua social unit, often translated as a ward or lineage group, that held land and organized labor, tribute and local ceremonies in Tenochtitlan. The city was built from many such units.

A raised field built in shallow lake water from mud, reeds and plants, used to grow maize and other crops around Tenochtitlan. Chinampas made the island city fertile and are still used in places like Xochimilco.

The language of the Nahua peoples and of the Mexica, still spoken by well over a million people in Mexico. Colonial texts such as the Florentine Codex and the Leyenda de los Soles were written in Nahuatl.
